channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Nvidia's Huang Says He Would Not Sell Chips to Irresponsible AI Customers
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang says his company would stop selling chips to a customer that was developing unsafe AI software. He talks extensively about AI safety and how the industry is growing with Bloomberg's Emily Chang in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CoreWeave’s Brazen Dream Crashes Into Reality as Yields Top 15%
item.description: For just about any company, it’d be an audacious thing to say: Find a way to get an investment-grade credit rating, and win access to “unlimited” funding.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Graf, Katherine Schwartz and Dina Bass

item.title: Arrested OpenAI Engineer Booked a One-Way Ticket to Saudi Arabia
item.description: The OpenAI employee who was arrested and charged with allegedly using a hidden recording device in one of the ChatGPT maker’s San Francisco offices had a one-way ticket to Saudi Arabia booked for Oct. 12, according to a court filing.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz

item.title: Caterpillar Shares Eye 30% Slump as Oil Bites, AI Rally Stalls
item.description: Caterpillar Inc. shares are on track to fall more than 30% from their record high as concerns about oil prices, bond yields and the future of the artificial intelligence trade roil the industrial sector.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Griffin

item.title: Meta’s Use of R&D Credits for Data Centers Probed by Democrats
item.description: Senate Democrats demanded answers from Meta Platforms, Inc. on whether it used a dubious tax strategy to reap billions in federal breaks to fund data center construction.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cioffi

item.title: CoreWeave CEO Says Market Acting ‘Irrationally,’ Stands by Model
item.description: CoreWeave Inc. Chief Executive Officer Mike Intrator, facing a plunge in the company’s stock and bond prices, said the market is acting “irrationally” and that he remains confident in the AI cloud company’s business model.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass

item.title: Inside the Making of ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’
item.description: GTA VI is set to release on November 19th, expected to be one of the biggest entertainment releases in history. The game, created by Rockstar Games, a development studio owned by Take-Two, is expected to generate more than $3 billion dollars in its first four months. Bloomberg's Jason Schreier joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech" with the details of the making of the highly anticipated game. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia CEO Says He Would Cut Off Customers Who Build Unsafe AI
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang said he would halt the supply of chips to a customer that was developing unsafe AI software, though he doesn’t believe that the current level of concern about the technology is warranted.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: AI Boom Drives ASML Higher as Nvidia Bets on Europe
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down ASML's earnings after the company raised its sales forecast for 2026 and said it aims to increase production of its chip-making machines to keep up with soaring AI spending. Plus, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announces plans to invest an additional $2 billion in European deals. And, an inside look at the making of Grand Theft Auto VI, expected to be the biggest video game blockbuster of all time. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US, Chinese Robotaxi Rivals Race for Europe
item.description: Europe is emerging as a key battleground for the global robotaxi industry as US and Chinese companies look to expand autonomous driving beyond their home markets. Frank McCleary, a partner at Arthur D. Little, discusses Europe’s fragmented but evolving regulatory landscape, why Chinese operators see an opportunity there as the US remains largely closed to them, and whether experience gained deploying autonomous vehicles in China translates to cities overseas. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Modal CEO: AI Has Entered a ‘New Era of Software’
item.description: AI cloud startup Modal has raised $750 million at a $15.75 billion post-money valuation as demand surges for the infrastructure needed to build and run AI applications. CEO Erik Bernhardsson discusses the company’s more than 3 billion AI sandboxes, growing demand for inference and reinforcement learning, and why increasingly capable agents will need secure virtual environments where they can execute code and eventually take on longer-running tasks. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI Employee Arrested Over Hidden Recording Device
item.description: An OpenAI employee has been arrested and accused of planting a hidden recording device inside an executive conference room at the company’s San Francisco offices. Bloomberg’s Rachel Metz discusses the FBI investigation, how the inexpensive device was discovered and OpenAI’s response. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ASML Struggles to Keep Up With High AI Demand
item.description: ASML is racing to expand capacity as demand for the advanced chipmaking equipment needed to power the AI boom stretches years into the future. Intesa Sanpaolo analyst Antonella Frongillo discusses why semiconductor equipment makers are already talking with customers about demand into 2029 and 2030, and why she sees further upside for ASML despite uncertainty around its China business and new regulatory restrictions. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hackers Hit Fridge Vendor Before Temperatures Soared in French Stores
item.description: Danfoss previously released patches for the vulnerabilities.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gallagher

item.title: CoreWeave, Neocloud Leverage a Concern for Gil Luria
item.description: Gil Luria, head of technology research at DA Davidson, says CoreWeave is “destroying value at every turn” if the company is “borrowing at 9% and the best return they can get off of that is a 5% return, it doesn’t matter how much they scale.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Inflation Rises as Fuel Costs Surge
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Vonnie Quinn on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Inflation heats up as fuel prices risev and Middle East tensions threaten more pressure ahead. Big bank earnings expose a divide on Wall Street. RBC’s Gerard Cassidy breaks down rates, margins and credit risk. Plus, AI demand keeps surging. Stripe Vice Chair Eileen O’Mara on Europe’s startup push and how agentic commerce could transform payments. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iowa, Michigan Hit by Weak Exports Ahead of Tight Midterm Races
item.description: Iowa and Michigan are among US states with competitive Senate races that appear hardest hit by President Donald Trump’s tariff agenda, with exports falling relative to before his second term began.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Diaz

item.title: OpenAI Names Ruddarraju to Lead Data Center, Computing Unit
item.description: OpenAI has named former xAI executive Uday Ruddarraju to lead its infrastructure and compute businesses, marking the latest leadership shakeup for its teams focused on expanding data center capacity.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass

item.title: GlobalFoundries Gets $21 Billion for Plants in US-Japan Deal
item.description: GlobalFoundries Inc. plans to build two new chip plants with the backing of as much as $21 billion from the Japanese government, part of an arrangement that also includes the US taking a 4% stake in the company.
item.dc:creator: Ian King and Maggie Eastland

item.title: Apple-OpenAI Judge Says He’s ‘Likely’ to Side With iPhone Maker
item.description: The judge in Apple Inc.’s high-stakes trade-secret theft case against OpenAI said he’s “highly likely” to grant the iPhone maker an injunction barring use of its proprietary information by former employees now at the artificial intelligence startup.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman, Annelise Levy (Bloomberg Law) and Georgia Fearn
